comparison: Both strongly support the core finding of a reproductive continuum with widespread clonal gamete production across hybrids. OpenEval cites 19 F1 families and cytological evidence (C39-C61), while peer reviewers describe evidence as 'compelling' and 'rigorous.' High agreement on claims C3, C4, C76-C78, C83, C85, though peer review also includes C84, C86.

Both support chromosome pairing defects in hybrids. OpenEval emphasizes detailed cytological analysis showing ~0.7% endoreplication at pachytene vs 100% at diplotene (C62, C66). Peer reviewers accept findings on aberrant pairing (C5, C51, C59, C102) and describe cytogenetic work as 'beautiful,' though they focus more on C115-C116 regarding male arrest.

Both support the endoreplication rescue mechanism. OpenEval details the pachytene-diplotene transition with immunofluorescence data (C54-C55, C61, C103-C104). Peer review R3 explicitly endorses 'premeiotic genome endoreplication is the mechanism behind asexually-reproducing females' with strong evidence. Substantial overlap on mechanism claims C6, C54-C55, C61, C66-C67, C103-C104.

Both support cytological characterization of hybrids using flow cytometry, histology, and chromosome analysis. OpenEval cites 244 analyzed cells (C48-C52, C107, C113-C114). Peer reviewers accept these findings as part of 'impressively detailed characterization of gametogenesis.' Strong agreement on C48-C50, C113-C114.

Perfect claim overlap (C71-C75, C108-C109, C119). Both support GLMM statistical analysis showing negative correlations between karyotype divergence, genetic distance, sex effects and bivalent formation. OpenEval provides specific statistics (z-values, p-values), peer reviewers note 'analyses are sound' and highlight 'previously overlooked effect of chromosome organisation on speciation.'

Both support low endoreplication frequency at pachytene with selective progression to diplotene. OpenEval emphasizes statistical comparisons (GLM, p-values) and 792 analyzed oocytes showing 0% in parentals (C62-C69, C121-C122). Peer review accepts quantitative findings and comparison with natural clones as 'convincing.' Overlap on C62-C65, C121-C122.

Both support widespread emergence of asexual gametogenesis across phylogenetically diverse crosses. OpenEval cites experimental data showing pattern doesn't depend on particular parental genome (C8-C9, C22, C90-C91, C93-C94, C126). Peer reviewers identify this as 'a key finding' requiring consideration of other factors to explain rarity of asexual species. Agreement on C88-C94.

Both support the conceptual link between hybrid asexuality and speciation continuum. OpenEval notes broader evolutionary interpretation involves inference (C8-C9, C22, C126). Peer reviewers endorse framework as providing 'important insights' about 'potential for asexuality to evolve during a relatively wide window of species divergence.' Partial overlap on C8-C9, C126.

Both support identical endoreplication mechanism across all clonal F1 females with properly formed bivalents. OpenEval cites cytological analysis (C61, C95-C96) consistent with natural asexual vertebrates. Peer reviewers find evidence 'strong' for premeiotic genome endoreplication as general mechanism. Agreement on C95-C96.

Both support phylogenetic and karyotype characterization. OpenEval details Mantel test, karyotype data, and non-linearity from convergent evolution (C36-C38). Peer reviewers accept this framework as foundation for experimental design, praising approach of 'analysing meiotic processes across different levels of divergence.' Agreement on C34-C38.

Both support experimental design and basic outcomes. OpenEval cites 19 F1 families, 12 species combinations, no sex ratio bias (C39-C41). Peer reviewers implicitly accept by describing experiments as 'rigorous' and 'impressively detailed.' Agreement on C40-C41 as methodological foundation.

Both support findings on NP hybrids showing 25 bivalents at pachytene and diplotene, representing exceptions to general pattern. OpenEval notes inference about orthologous vs homologous pairing is reasonable but not directly proven (C56, C58, C82). Peer reviewers accept these as part of continuum concept. Perfect agreement on C56, C58, C82.

Perfect claim overlap (C79-C80, C117-C118, C120, C124, C130). Both support correlation between karyotype divergence and reproductive mode. OpenEval notes mechanistic interpretation involves inference from correlational data. Peer review R15 explicitly highlights 'previously overlooked effect of chromosome organisation on speciation' as central to explaining rarity of asexual lineages.

Perfect claim overlap (C110-C112). Both support sex-specific differences in bivalent formation and cite transplantation experiments. OpenEval notes mechanistic interpretation is inferential and transplantation data from cited study. Peer reviewers accept as part of overall findings on 'effect of chromosome organisation on speciation.'

Both support detrimental impact of aberrant pairing in both sexes. OpenEval cites cytological analysis showing similar patterns (C59, C115-C116) but females have rescue mechanism. Peer review R2 accepts chromosome pairing defects and notes meiosis arrests in males. Agreement on C115-C116.

Both address hypotheses about rarity of natural asexual lineages despite frequent unreduced gamete production. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting selective filtering mechanism is speculative and not directly tested (C127, C131-C134). Peer reviewers SUPPORT the conceptual framework, calling it a resolution to 'a major unresolved issue.' Divergence in confidence level despite agreement on claims.

Both support lack of reciprocal cross effects (C64). OpenEval notes statistical test not explicitly stated, a minor limitation. Peer reviewers implicitly accept through endorsement of overall quantitative findings. Minimal overlap but consistent acceptance.

Both support quantitative assessment of asexual gametogenesis frequency. OpenEval cites experimental data and literature compilation (C88-C89). Peer review R5 identifies this as 'a key finding' about commonness of unreduced gametes. Agreement on C88-C89.

Both address prevailing view that manuscript challenges. OpenEval notes these claims (C1-C2, C23-C24, C125) represent field consensus requiring revision based on new data. Peer review R16 strongly endorses the challenge to previous assumptions as 'a key finding' of 'broad interest.' Agreement on C1-C2, C23, C125, C135-C136.

Both support absence of endoreplication in parental species. OpenEval cites 792 analyzed oocytes showing 0% (C69, C100-C101) as important negative control. Peer review R4 finds evidence 'convincing that this phenomenon is a consequence of combining two divergent genomes in an F1 hybrid female.' Agreement on C100-C101.

OpenEval supports immunofluorescence, flow cytometry, and histology methods (C42-C47) with 852 parental cells as baseline controls. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though methods are implicitly accepted through reviewers' endorsement of overall experimental rigor.

OpenEval supports phylogenetic context (C34-C35, C25-C29) based on exome-wide SNP data and published studies. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though this background is implicitly accepted as foundation for experimental design.

OpenEval supports established knowledge about natural Cobitidae hybrid systems (C30-C33) with multiple citations. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though this context is implicitly accepted.

OpenEval supports comparative context from other hybrid systems (C105-C106) based on citations, noting inference about 'successfully established' asexuals extends beyond direct evidence. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval supports theoretical frameworks from literature (C10-C16, C19-C21) as conceptual context. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though these background concepts underpin the interpretations reviewers endorse.

OpenEval supports range of reproductive outcomes across phylogenetic spectrum (C84, C86-C87) including TP hybrid data from literature. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though continuum concept is endorsed by reviewers.
OpenEval supports comparative context suggesting phenomenon may be general across vertebrates (C92) based on citation to Iwai et al. 2011. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN the speculation about relative ease of different asexual pathways (C97-C99), noting C99 lacks direct experimental evidence. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval supports ~6% endoreplication in natural clones (C123) based on previously published data, noting source should be more explicitly cited. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though comparison with natural clones is accepted by reviewers.

OpenEval supports description of tension between balance hypothesis predictions (C128) and empirical observations (C129), highlighting paradox motivating proposed resolution. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though reviewers endorse the resolution framework.

OpenEval supports specific examples of karyotype diversity (C137-C138) illustrating why AKD is important metric. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though karyotype framework is accepted by reviewers.
